issues.issue: The script silently ignores flags it does not know. If someone types `--rules=5` or `--rule 5` after the URL, the gate posts the five paid calls without the rules version check and without the version 5 send-back gate, and can exit 0 on version 4 answers. The base script also ignored unknown flags, but `--rules` is now the switch that makes the gate meaningful.
issues.evidence: In `const base = args.find((arg, k) => !arg.startsWith("--") && !VALUED.has(args[k - 1]))` and `valueOf("--rules")`, `--rules=5` matches neither, so `rules` stays null. Every check in `if (rules !== null) { ... }` is then skipped, and the run ends with `process.exitCode = stop ? 1 : 0`, where `stop` reflects only non-200 answers.
issues.fix: Reject any argument that starts with `--` and is not `--dry`, `--rules` or `--from`, with usage(`unknown flag ...`) and exit 2. Optionally also accept the `--rules=<n>` form.

deviations: The spoken clock line heuristic (spokenClockLine) is not in the spec. A line the parser reads as a speaker at a clock's colon (`Tuesday at 2:30 works for me.` read as a speaker `Tuesday at 2`) is read as words only when it is the exception. Four conditions must all hold: (1) its label colon is a clock colon; (2) its label heads no line with a text colon; (3) its key, the label with its trailing 1 to 3 digits removed, heads fewer than 2 clock colon lines of the input; (4) outside header mode, clock colon lines (clockColon with nameClock true) are fewer than a quarter of the non-blank input lines. Under accepted headers, rule 4 is skipped. Where any condition fails, the parser's label is kept and written `Label: text` (for example `2026-10-03 15: 02 Sam: Hi.`), so a second pass reads the same thing. The spoken lines it finds are counted lone_headers. Reason: I3, a spoken line is never a speaker, without taking away labels the parser reads today.

N1 (1.10 says unchanged) is changed: `Call me at 2:30` among speaker lines becomes words of the turn above, with lone_headers 1. T19 (four ISO-dated chat lines) is now returned as given with the parser's speaker `2026-10-03 15`, because that key heads every line. T17 now reads its two header-like lines with the parser's labels.

Form d also takes its words on the header line: `^(NAME)([ \t]+)(TIME)(?:[ \t]+(\S.*))?$`. With words on the line, only one space or a tab is form d (always weak). Two or more spaces are left to the parser's NAME_CLOCK_TURN (h). Form d counts names_joined only when no words follow the time on its line, as forms a and c do. Pinned by P8, P10 and P18. Reason: the verifier's recommended fix for issue 1, which keeps the names and the clocks.

clocks_joined, a 24th change code: it sits in CHANGE_CODES right after names_joined, and FACT_CODES grows from 9 to 10. In a timed_lines result it counts each turn whose clock stood on a line of its own, or after the name on the speaker's line, where names_joined does not already count the header. Cases: a bare clock joined to a labelled line, a bare clock attached to a form f or g header, forms a, c and d with words on the header line, the parser's name and clock lines, and cue turns written as timed lines. The clock entry carries `joined: true` in the ledger (JavaScript only). Reason: a changed result never carries an empty changes list (I3, I4); P12, P13 and P14 previously had empty lists.

S6 rules 2, 3 and 4 run until no candidate changes, not 2, 3, 4, 2, 3 once. Candidates only move out of the counted state, so the loop ends. Reason: the fuzzer found invariant 7 failures where a second rule 3 pass returned a form to h after rule 2 had already run.

Cue ids: digits and UUIDs (with Teams' `/n-n` tail) as S4 writes them. Word ids are allowed only in a file whose first non-blank line starts with WEBVTT, after a blank line, as WebVTT defines them (pinned by P4). If that first scan used a word id and finds plain lines with letters or digits outside every cue (a mixed paste), the cues are read again without word ids, so the spoken line stays (P19). Outside WEBVTT files a spoken line before a timing line stays, and the paste is mixed (P11).

Form b takes a trailing parenthetical of any length, the empty one included; S6 says 1 to 48. Reason: a line that opens with a clock and ` - ` is not prose. Enforcing 48 made a speaker with a long company name lose every header, so their lines became words of the other speaker's turn. Pinned by P15. Form f keeps 1 to 48, counted in code points.

Every pattern with a counted repeat now carries the u flag, so it counts code points as Python's re does (1.12): FORM_A, FORM_B, FORM_C, FORM_D, FORM_F, FORM_G, TITLED, ISO_DATE, MARKER, CLOSED_TAG. Before, JavaScript counted UTF-16 units there.
CLOSED_TAG's tag body is bounded to `[^>]{0,200}`, and angle text is tested with two scans (`indexOf('<')`, then `lastIndexOf('>') > it`) instead of `/<.*>/`, so both are linear.

Kept from the earlier round and recorded here for I2: TURN_LINE_RULES adds date_only, not date. date_only is a whole line ISO or month date with an optional time and nothing after it, which the parser reads as a turn (`2026-10-03 15:02`, `Oct 3 2026 3:02 PM`, pinned by T7 and P16); the looser date rule never removes a turn line. A date is never a NAME. A bare clock above a header zone line is removed with the header block under rule `clock` (P6). A fix that reads as nothing where the input read as turns returns the input as given (the safety net).

Speed: the 5.1 bound is under 2 s. When the parser's own read of the same text takes over 400 ms, which only happens on a loaded shared machine, the formatter is held to 8 times that read instead (fastEnough in format.test.js). A cue payload of many `<` with no `>` stays quadratic in the parser's own TAGS pattern, so that case is tested as a ratio: the formatter takes at most 3 times the parser plus 50 ms.

Last round's issue 1 is fixed only for a single spoken clock line. In every export shape of 1.10, two spoken lines that open with the same word and a clock ("At 2:30 we have the board meeting." ... Rule 4 of S6 then finds the speaker's real header empty and removes it (strong forms a and g) or leaves it as words of the turn above (weak forms b, c and e).

Its clock then goes to S8, and the whole call is untimed (clocks_backwards).
The invariants cannot see either effect: invariant 7 is satisfied because the fake speaker heads 2 turns, and invariant 6 allows empty_header removals. The change list tells the rep that speaker names with no words were removed, which is misleading. The spec as written also fails this input, because S7 keeps form h labels. That makes this an incomplete fix of the I3 promise the builder claimed for issue 1, not a regression against the spec.
